<issue_description>
php_fgetcsv in ext/standard/file.c (invoked via zif_str_getcsv) can compute an incorrect copy length and pass a negative size to memcpy (ASAN negative-size-param). This leads to an invalid memcpy call that can cause memory corruption/heap overflow and crashes when parsing specially crafted CSV input, potentially enabling denial-of-service or other memory-safety issues.

import cpp

from FunctionCall call, Expr arg2
where call.getTarget().getName() = "memcpy" and
      call.getEnclosingFunction().getName() = "php_fgetcsv" and
      call.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath() = "ext/standard/file.c" and
      arg2 = call.getArgument(2)
select call.getLocation(), "memcpy size arg: " + arg2.toString()

      sub = call.getArgument(2) and
      sub.getOperator() = "-"
select call.getLocation(), "Potentially-negative memcpy length: " + sub.toString()
